purpose: Bring the two one-time credential lifetimes under the ceilings ASVS 5.0 V6.5.5 sets: a TOTP is accepted for its own 30-second step and no longer, and the out-of-band MFA-recovery credential lives 10 minutes rather than 30. The mail that tells a user how long the recovery link lasts is made to read the delivered lifetime instead of restating a number.
requiredInvariants: No database schema change. expires_at was already computed from the constant, so lowering the constant needs no migration and no backfill; challenges already minted keep the expiry they were issued with and simply age out.

Narrowing the TOTP window is not replay protection and is not presented as any. The same code presented twice inside its own step still verifies twice - that is V6.5.1, it needs durable per-user state, and it stays open under #4682.

The TOTP change is a deliberate divergence from RFC 6238 s5.2, which recommends allowing at most one step of drift. ASVS 5.0 V6.5.5 sets 30 seconds. The two disagree; the stricter bound is taken and the tradeoff is written down at the constant rather than buried, because a device whose clock is off by more than a step stops being able to log in by TOTP.

The invitation credential keeps its 72-hour lifetime and is not touched. It admits nobody on its own and starts a review by a human administrator, so it is not an out-of-band authentication request; the cap belongs to the credential that completes an authentication.

The registration email-verification link keeps its 30-minute lifetime and is not touched. It proves control of an address during registration rather than authenticating an existing account, and it sits on the PC-CROP registration path this pass is required not to disturb.

The MFA-recovery mail copy is derived from the delivered expiresInSeconds and clamped to the ceiling, so it can understate the lifetime but never overstate it. A delivery arriving without a lifetime falls back to the ceiling rather than guessing.

apps/api/src/modules/auth-mail/auth-mail-templates.ts's mfaRecoveryMail has no callers anywhere in the repository - the mail that reaches a mailbox is built web-side. It is not deleted, because a template is not a control and deleting it removes no enforcement; it is given a required lifetime argument so it can no longer carry a stale hardcoded one.

apps/api/src/modules/mfa/mfa.service.ts holds a second verifyTotp with the same wide window and is deliberately not touched here. It persists nothing and is not a live pathway, so changing it would prove nothing about enforcement; the decorative module is a separate pass.
apps/landing is not touched. No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation.

The cryptographic inventory is regenerated by script, not edited: main carries scannedFiles 2168 while the tree holds 2169, because the presentation contour added a source file without regenerating. That staleness fails discover-cryptography.test.mjs on clean main and on every pull request touching apps/** or the ASVS decisions, so it blocks this branch technically rather than incidentally. PR #4760 carries the identical one-line regeneration; whichever of the two lands second will find it already applied. No file belonging to the presentation contour is touched here.
acceptance: The production TOTP implementation agrees with the RFC 6238 Appendix B published vectors, checked through the real verifier rather than against a copy of itself.
A code from the previous step and a code from the next step are both refused, and a code is accepted for the whole of its own step and not one millisecond past it.
Restoring the three-step window fails 4 of the 10 API cases; restoring the 30-minute TTL fails 1; restoring the 30-minute mail ceiling fails 2 of the 8 web cases.
The recovery mail states the lifetime it was handed, in ru, en and zh, declines the Russian plural correctly, and says thirty minutes in no language.
The matrix rebuilds with V6.5.5 moved to PASS under conditions that revoke it if either ceiling is widened again.
